tasks.design: Configure a native shift-log form in {OPS_SYSTEM}, so the operator captures observations once and the system stores that entry directly. Preserve observation, field capture and checking time; remove only later re-entry of the same values.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper logs can require a second entry into the production database.
tasks.enabler_now: Native electronic forms can store typed readings and production quantities at capture.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong units, wrong batches and questionable readings still require human checking.
tasks.human_edge: The operator determines whether a value reflects the process or an observation problem.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate typing, with the same responsibility for reliable process records.

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs for SPC; this supports connected production-data capability, not this plant's log savings.
Replacing duplicate shift-log entry with a native form and the estimated savings are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is operator logging; acquiring lab test results and physically monitoring or operating equipment are separate existing work, not additional savings here.

In s1 the operator produces batch ID, equipment ID, shift, timestamp, reading type, numeric value, unit, result source and missing-value reason. All 50 hours remain, including capture. Missing fields or unavailable devices use paper capture and later manual entry; no extraction is assumed free.
Test native forms and store-on-submit before code. Do not claim automatic sensor collection or classify process compliance from the log.
Allow five focal hours for field corrections, form upkeep and fallback reconciliation beyond routine s3 checks. No new other-role curation is required.
